note: Web research. Every entry carries a confidence rating; corrections below were raised by the researcher against the briefing premise and MUST be read before use.
corrections: ⛔ BRIEFING ERROR (mine): I told the researcher andel's occupies a converted SCHEIBLER mill in Manufaktura. Wrong. Manufaktura is the POZNAŃSKI complex; Scheibler's empire is Księży Młyn, a separate site across the city. Do not let this conflation reach the roster — the two dynasties are distinct and it is exactly the kind of error a confident guide propagates.
andel's Hotel is officially renamed 'Vienna House by Wyndham Andel's Lodz'; locals still say andel's.
Muzeum Archeologiczne i Etnograficzne is EFFECTIVELY CLOSED — under modernization since 2025, one temporary exhibition only. Do not describe permanent displays as visitable.
The Loom is at Ogrodowa 21 by Manufaktura, NOT on Piotrkowska.
Teatr Szwalnia moved to Struga 90 and reports financial/premises instability — verify before publishing (confidence: medium).
Kino Polonia currently brands as 'Kino Polonia Reaktywacja'; Kino Wytwórnia is usually listed as 'Kino 3D Wytwórnia'.

entries.name: Muzeum Sztuki MS1
entries.blurb: Original site of Muzeum Sztuki at Więckowskiego 36 (entrance Gdańska 43), founded 1931 from the a.r. group's International Collection of Modern Art. Focuses on 20th-century work.
entries.why_notable: Europe's first and the world's second museum dedicated to modern art, after MoMA.

entries.name: Muzeum Sztuki MS2
entries.blurb: Second branch at Ogrodowa 19 in the Manufaktura complex, opened 2008. Four halls holding the permanent collection display 'Ways of Seeing' plus temporary exhibitions.
entries.why_notable: Houses the main permanent presentation of the Muzeum Sztuki collection.

entries.name: Muzeum Archeologiczne i Etnograficzne w Łodzi
entries.blurb: At plac Wolności 14 since 1956, descended from the 1918 City Museum. Roughly 290,000 objects across archaeology, ethnography, numismatics and puppet theatre.
entries.why_notable: Largest museum in Łódź by holdings; currently closed for modernization.

entries.name: Muzeum Tradycji Niepodległościowych w Łodzi
entries.blurb: Main site at Gdańska 13 in an 1883–85 prison used through both wars and until 1953. Branches at Radogoszcz and Stacja Radegast.
entries.why_notable: Łódź's longest-running history museum; the Radegast branch marks the Litzmannstadt Ghetto deportation station.

entries.name: Teatr Wielki (Łódź)
entries.blurb: Opera and ballet house on plac Dąbrowskiego, built 1949–1964 and opened 19 January 1967 with Moniuszko's 'Halka'. Auditorium seats 1,074 since the 2003 renovation.
entries.why_notable: One of Europe's largest opera stages; among the most modern in the world at opening.

entries.name: Filharmonia Łódzka
entries.blurb: Artur Rubinstein Philharmonic at Narutowicza 20/22. Current building by Romuald Loegler opened 10 December 2004, replacing the demolished hall; 658-seat concert hall plus a chamber hall.
entries.why_notable: Won SARP's award for best publicly funded building of 2004.

entries.name: Teatr Szwalnia
entries.blurb: Independent theatre, now at Struga 90, working without a permanent ensemble or stable funding. Small-scale, close-contact staging with an emphasis on acting craft.
entries.why_notable: Long-running anchor of Łódź's off-theatre scene, roughly 15 years old.

entries.name: Kino Polonia
entries.blurb: Art-house cinema at Piotrkowska 67, on a site with film exhibition dating to 1911. Run by the Polish Filmmakers Association; mainly Polish and European programming.
entries.why_notable: Hosts Camerimage and Sputnik festival screenings; a pillar of the SFP art-house network.

entries.name: Kino Wytwórnia
entries.blurb: 169-seat cinema at Łąkowa 29, entrance B, built inside studio hall 10A of the former Wytwórnia Filmów Fabularnych. Part of the Klub Wytwórnia venue.
entries.why_notable: Occupies the feature-film studio that produced hundreds of Polish films, 1945–1998.

entries.name: andel's Hotel Łódź
entries.blurb: Four-star hotel opened 2009 in the former Izrael Poznański spinning mill at Manufaktura. Now trades as Vienna House by Wyndham Andel's Lodz.
entries.why_notable: Widely cited industrial-conversion hotel; red-brick mill structure kept and exposed throughout.

entries.name: The Loom
entries.blurb: Four-star hotel at Ogrodowa 21 beside Manufaktura, opened to guests 1 April 2022. 76 rooms, with interiors themed on the Łódź textile industry.
entries.why_notable: One of the newest hotels in the Manufaktura area.

entries.name: Hala Górniak
entries.blurb: Market hall on plac Niepodległości, built 1932–34 to Paweł Sperr's design with an all-timber roof. Now around 148 indoor stalls plus 50 outdoor.
entries.why_notable: One of Łódź's two oldest markets; location for Machulski's film 'Kingsajz'.
